INTERVIEW
EXPERIENCE
Akshay Phalke

2
Eligibility Criteria : A total of 98 students were eligible
For All Students, CGPA criteria was 7+.
Only CS, IT & Extc. were allowed to apply.
Online Assessment
6th November, 2022
The proctored online assessment was conducted on the HackerEarth platform. Total time allotted was
90 minutes. There were 2 coding questions and 10 MCQs based on Core CS fundamentals. OA(Online
Assessment) comprised 90 Points in total. It was a proctored test that required camera permissions.
Changing tabs would lead to being flagged.
1. Collecting Coins - 30 Points
John is playing a battle game in which the game consists of N heroes and M monsters. The powers of
heroes and the monsters are represented by arrays A and B respectively. A hero can defeat a monster
if his power is greater than equal to the power of the monster. A hero gains some number of coins
corresponding to the monster he defeated. The coins after defeating a particular monster are
represented by an array C of size M.
Now, John is curious to know how many coins each hero can collect by defeating any monster in the
game. You are asked to return an array of N integers containing coins earned by each hero.
Note:
●
The health of a hero doesn’t get reduced after defeating a monster.
●
A monster can be defeated by multiple heroes.
Akshay Phalke | Deutsche Bank Interview Experience 2022

3
Consider the following testcase:
Let N = 5    M = 4    A = [1,3,5,2,4]    B = [1,4,2,9]
C = [1,2,8,4]
Approach:
The first hero can defeat only the 1st monster, so he gains only 1 coin.
The second hero can defeat the 1st and 3rd monsters, so he gains 1+8=9 coins.
Similarly the third, fourth, and fifth hero gains 11, 9, 11 coins respectively.
Return: [ 1, 9, 11, 9, 11 ]
My approach to question:
Initially, I Solved the question through brute force method as it is quite an obvious one.
For each hero you should traverse the whole monster’s array i.e use two FOR loops and traverse hero array in
outer loop and traverse monsters’ array in inner loop. But this solution led me to the TLE(Time Limit Exceed). I
was able to pass just 6 out of 12 test cases.
No programmer wishes to see TLE for his/her submission. I went on thinking about optimizing my approach and I
had already wasted 10-15 mins for the previous solution. After trying my ways for optimizing for about 5-10 mins, I
discovered that I can use binary search.But the task was we cannot sort the monsters’ directly because then we
could not find the corresponding points earned after defeating the specific monster. I then had an idea of using a
vector pair of monster’s energy and points to be gained after defeating that specific monster. But using binary
on it was not that easy. You need to sort the vector pair using the comparator function, so you should know how
the comparator function works. I sorted the vector pair, applied binary search for each hero on the monster's
array and added the coins gained to the “ans” variable of every loop after defeating the specific monster. Finally,
I was able to pass 12 / 12 test cases.
2. Maximum Quirkiness - 20 points
You are given an array A of size N. You need to select distinct indexes such that the quirkiness
between them is maximum.
The Quirkiness  of two indexes i and j is defined Q( i, j ) = Sum from i from to j inclusive + c * ( j - i )
More Formally, you need to print the maximum value of Q( i, j ) =
Akshay Phalke | Deutsche Bank Interview Experience 2022

4
Consider the following testcase:
Let N = 3    c=1    A = [1, 2, 3]
Approach:
Here, if you take i=1 and j=3 , you get the quirkiness equal to 6 + 1 * ( 3 - 1 ) = 8.
This is the maximum quirkiness across all pairs of indexes.
Return: 8
My approach to question:
Changing value while calculating quirkiness is Sum and ( j- i ). As we need to get maximum quirkiness, we need
to find the maximum value of ( j- i ) and maximum sum between j and i. And constraint that index j should come
after index i. A simple solution to this problem I applied was using two for loops. For each i you calculate
quirkiness across every j in inner loop .This solution led to TLE as in the previous question.
I then went on optimizing the problem's solution. After trying many test cases on my own, I found out that an
answer is possible in one for loop but I was not totally sure about it. I applied one for loop with i variable and
maintained sum, currentsum, ans, count variable throughout the loop. I added A[ i ] to sum variable and
incremented count for each iteration. Thus, calculated currentsum = sum + c * ( i - count) and if currentsum<0  i
updated sum=0 and count=0 ,as we can get elements with more sum later on in the loop.At last of each iteration
I updated ans = max ( ans, currentsum). Finally, I was able to pass 10/12 test cases.
This question took more time than expected, almost 25-30 minutes.
3-12. MCQs on CS Fundamentals - 40 points
It consisted of 10 MCQs about CS Fundamentals. It asked about the OS, OOPs, DBMS, CN, and a few
debugging/output-related questions. The questions were either easy or moderate, and the only concern was the
time constraint. The questions covered the main topics from every subject.
The results of the online assessment were released after 2 days on 8th November, 2022. A total
of 11 students were shortlisted for the interviews.
Akshay Phalke | Deutsche Bank Interview Experience 2022

5
Technical Round
9th November, 2022
9.30 am - 10.15 am
The interview started at 9.30 with the standard question “Tell me about yourself”. Have some pointers
ready in your mind to answer this question as this part is very important. Based on your introduction, the
interviewer might ask you certain questions.This round was conducted on Skype.
In my introduction, I told him about my experiences as a MERN developer. The Tech stacks I used and am
proficient in. I told him about the hackathons I had attended and my projects. He then asked me some
questions on my resume and coding platforms where I often use to code.
He then moved to OS and asked me the difference between process and thread.It was a pretty simple
question to be asked initially. He went on asking me regarding Process Control Block(PCB) and types of
threads and how they are different. In the next question he moved to OOPs concepts where i was asked
to explain different types of polymorphism and how they occur. I went on explaining to him about runtime
and compile time polymorphism.
Moving on to DBMS, he first inquired about the ACID properties and their significance. He told me that
you have an employee table with four columns (fields), namely employeeId, employeeName,
managerName, and dateOfJoining of employees. He asked me to create a SQL query in the notepad to
find employees who joined after the manager's dateOfJoining. The main crux here is that the manager is
also an employee. After hearing the question, I was slightly taken aback. I knew it was going to be a
nested query, and I hadn't done much practise with them. So I continued to ponder how this could be
accomplished. After 3-4 minutes of thinking and telling him sideways, I came up with a solution that wasn't
entirely correct, but it satisfied the interviewer. He was only interested in my approach and SQL
knowledge.
DSA QS - 10/15 mins
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/sort-an-array-of-0s-1s-and-2s/
I initially struggled with this one. I knew the brute force solution was in O(n2), but I couldn't get to the
optimal solution fast enough. I recall going over this question once but being unable to recall the exact
solution at the time. He asked me to share my screen and open a notepad to write the code assuming
my own test cases. I initially told him about the O(n2) solution. Then I moved on to an O(nlogn) solution,
i.e. sorting the array of 0s, 1s, and 2s, but he asked how efficiently I could sort this. Of course, the
merge sort is the most efficient sort method.I went on to demonstrate how the merge sort works on a
Akshay Phalke | Deutsche Bank Interview Experience 2022

6
notepad using actual examples. While telling him about this sorting method, the optimal solution of
using three variables, as used in the Dutch National Flag Algorithm, occurred to me. I soon told him the
best approach, and he was pleased with all of mine. The interviewer led the way throughout the
interview.
Note: If you know the best solution, don't tell the interviewer right away. Start with brute force and
then tell him/her about your optimal solution. Also tell time complexity for each solution you present.
Don't panic if you don’t remember any optimal answer or are not able to understand the approach.
Initially, always try to go through a brute force approach.
Out of the 11 students interviewed for Round 1, 3 students were shortlisted for the next round.
I was luckily one of them.
Professional Fitness Round
9th November, 2022
2.00 pm - 2.20 pm
PS: I had no idea what this round was about. But, prior to my interview, I learned from my colleague
(who is also chosen for the DB summer internship) that this round is fairly standard and that she was
asked basic HR questions. So I took this lightly and assumed it would be a casual HR round. But
after the interview, my opinions had shifted. For me, it was a completely technical round with even
more deep understanding questions than the previous one.
I was initially greeted by an interviewer. He then asked me to introduce myself. After which he
started asking me about my resume and one of my projects was discussed for about 10-15 minutes.
In it , I then mentioned the project's goal, the problems it solved, some notable features, and the
highlights of the technology stack used. Then he asked regarding socket.io , React JS knowledge
and he was getting deep in socket connection with client and server. Various hooks of React JS and
Virtual DOM concepts were also being asked to me by him.
As he knew that I introduced myself as a MERN Developer, he started with MongoDB. He asked me
Akshay Phalke | Deutsche Bank Interview Experience 2022

7
why I prefer NoSQL over SQL. Over to this I answered it pretty well. He then inquired about any
MongoDb work I'd done in any of my projects. I went on explaining to him every feature that I
implemented. I wasn’t yet finished, meanwhile he asked about real life applications  of MongoDb.
He was taking it deep and even asked me what cluster, collections, documents, schema means in
MongoDb. And he ended it by asking the “free cluster” size and maximum document size
permitted in MongoDb. As I knew MongoDb well, I answered almost every question he had asked.
As, “basic python” was mentioned in my resume, he said,  “as you know python, we will continue
with python,” but I quickly corrected him, saying that I was more familiar with cpp and only knew the
basics of python.So we started with cpp, and he asked if I solved DSA problems. And where exactly
do you solve them, and how many have you solved so far?  I responded that I use Leetcode the
most to practice questions. "Which data structures are you familiar with?" he asked. I explained both
linear and nonlinear data structures to him.He then inquired about the "Stack" Data Structure, such
as where it should be used, how it should be used, and how it should be implemented.  While it was
going fairly smoothly, he asked about real life use of stack in NodeJS ? At that point of time I was
almost blank. I began to ponder, recalling the use of queues but not stacks. I told him honestly that I
didn't know the answer.
Now, he began asking questions on Node JS and my experience in NodeJS. After about 4-5
minutes of explanation by me on REST API, Postman API he asked me to swap the numbers
without a third variable. I know it is an easy question but I was unable to recall at that moment. And
my Interview was going such a way that my confidence was getting low every time he asked a new
question. He then also asked about Authentication and Authorization in NodeJS and its difference.
I answered it patiently.
DSA QS - 5/10 mins
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/deletion-in-doubly-circular-linked-list/
Coming to the DSA question, it was a standard question where I was asked to delete a node in the
Doubly Circular Linked List. I was asked to open the notepad and write the code for it. As I already knew
the question, it was an easy question at the end of the interview.
Akshay Phalke | Deutsche Bank Interview Experience 2022

8
At the End
The overall round was meant to be finished in 20 minutes but it was almost about 45-50 minutes. Always be
patient in your interviews. At the end of the interview, I was asked if I had any questions for them. I asked how it
feels as an employee at Deutsche Bank and their favorite thing about DB. They answered in a very friendly
manner and even talked about their personal experiences.
The results of this round came at about 3.30 PM and all 3 students were selected for it.
HR Round
9th November, 2022
4.00 pm - 4.10 pm
The female interviewer greeted me and asked me to introduce myself. I introduced  myself and told
her about my achievements. She then asked about my family background. After which she asked a
well-known but crucial question: "Why do you want to join DB?" And what exactly are values at DB?
We had PPT in the morning, and I listened intently. In fact, after my second round, I practiced some
basic HR questions. It was totally normal and the HR  was extremely pleasant. This was the best round
since the morning.
The Final Results came at about 10 PM. In total, 3 of us (2 girls, 1 boy) were offered the internship.
And I was fortunate among them.
Akshay Phalke | Deutsche Bank Interview Experience 2022

9
Tips
Personal Note
Even if you don’t get selected in any of the interviews dont ever lose your hope. I personally got
rejected in 3 different companies’ interviews before getting selected for DB as an intern. Do
remember your preparation and hard work always pays off. I kept on trying and improving every time
I got rejected. It feels like ‘chor do yeh, sab moh maya hai’ after every rejection. Sometimes it's just a
dumb luck and sometimes you face biasedness in terms of interviewers or in terms of questions
asked. At the end I would say, Just believe in Yourself.
DSA
To understand Concepts - You can start with Abdul Bari course and Learn DP from Aditya Verma
To Practice - Leetcode Daily Challenge, Leetcode Weekly Contests
To Follow - Striver’s 180 Sheet, 450 DSA Cracker
Core CS (OS, DBMS, OOPS)
OS - Gate Smashers will help in academics as well as interviews.
DBMS - Sachit Jain’s DBMS Playlist
CN - Neso Academy and Gate Smashers
Related to Interviews:
1. Trust yourself and your preparation.
2. Speak up without hesitation. Be a good communicator and listener. Go on clearing any doubts
you have throughout the interview.
3. Stay hydrated and isolated during the interview. Take short walks or breaks in between.
4. Be very cool, calm, collected and confident.
All the best!
Akshay Phalke | Deutsche Bank Interview Experience 2022
